summary: Run 4 of M1-S03 — a § 4 test-only repair after reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 6 (S2-F-11): the package compiled clean but every one of 28 test methods across the step's three test classes failed at execution, because none carried a System.runAs block for a permissioned user while Tier2WebhookQueueable and CaseTriggerHandler enforce the running user's FLS with WITH USER_MODE. The step's six non-test classes and both triggers are untouched — this run's scope is the tests' running-user context and setup only. templates/apex/tests/TestUserFactory.cls was copied verbatim into artefacts/M1-S03/classes/ with its meta XML; each of Tier2EscalationServiceTest, Tier2WebhookQueueableTest and IntegrationFailureResendTest gained PERM_SET/PROFILE constants, a TestUserFactory.createUser() call folded into the existing mixed-DML setup-object fence, a re-queried agent() helper, and every existing @IsTest method's body wrapped in System.runAs(agent()) — same statements, same assertions, same messages, nothing added or removed. skills/apex/test-class-standards/scripts/check_test_class_standards.py --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S03 now reports 0 findings (was the target rule, user-mode-test-without-runas); the three previously-declared checkers were re-run unchanged and still exit 0; check-outputs is ok on all 20 declared paths. deploy-order.md gained § 0b recording the repair, the run count, and the § 1/§ 2/§ 9 table updates for the new TestUserFactory member. The literal request to add TestUserFactory to 'the step's package.xml' was not carried out: this apex-builder-owned step has never declared a package.xml (standards/build-orchestration.md § 5, the Apex exception) and one would contradict that recorded exception plus § 4 condition 2; the new ApexClass member belongs at the build-level manifest step M1-S05 instead, which this run flags but does not touch.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM per GATES.md Gate D: Gate B resolved every symbol this run touches (TestUserFactory.createUser, Profile/PermissionSet/PermissionSetAssignment fields, all copied from the template or from standard-object grounding) and Gate C check 3 (compile) did not run — build_mode is design-only, there is no target_org_alias, and there is no offline Apex compiler in the sf CLI. Unlike run 3's MEDIUM, no attested-but-illegal identifier is at stake here; the fix is a mechanical application of a documented pattern (Example 5) the checker itself now verifies at 0 findings. What would raise this to HIGH is a green dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests or RunLocalTests, which no agent in this loop may perform.

findings.title: PROFILE = 'Standard User' is a default, not a grounded fact
findings.detail: No clarification in this build names a Profile for the users who can escalate a Case — Q19 names three admins by role ('Support Engineering admins'), not by profile. 'Standard User' is used because it is a real standard Salesforce profile present in every org and is the exact value skills/apex/test-class-standards/references/examples.md Example 5 uses for this same class. If the target org's escalating users hold a different profile, PROFILE is the one line to change in each of the three test classes before UAT.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the actual profile(s) of the users Tier2_Webhook_Admin is assigned to (deploy-order.md § 10 item 2) and update PROFILE if it differs from 'Standard User'. Does not block this repair: the checker and the pattern do not depend on which real profile is named, only that one exists in the target org.
